STM32F103C8T6.density_class: medium-density (64–128 KB range per PM0075 Glossary, p.5)

STM32F103CBT6.density_class: medium-density (64–128 KB range per PM0075 Glossary, p.5)

supported_external_interfaces: Boot loader (USART1, System memory boot mode)
In-application programming (IAP) via any on-chip communication interface
option_byte_unlock_keys: Same KEY1 = 0x45670123 and KEY2 = 0xCDEF89AB, written to FLASH_OPTKEYR (0x40022008)
page_erase_sequence: 1. Check BSY bit (PM p.14 text says 'FLASH_CR register' – apparent typo; BSY is in FLASH_SR per §3.4 p.25 and Figure 2 p.15)
3. Write page start address to FLASH_AR (0x40022014)
5. Wait for BSY bit in FLASH_SR to clear
mass_erase_sequence: 4. Wait for BSY bit in FLASH_SR to clear
program_sequence: 3. Perform 16-bit (half-word) write to target Flash address
4. Wait for BSY bit in FLASH_SR to clear
5. Read back and verify programmed value
programming.busy_flag: FLASH_SR bit 0 – BSY (Busy); set at start, cleared at end or on error
programming.end_of_operation_flag: FLASH_SR bit 5 – EOP (End of Operation); set at end of each successful program/erase; cleared by writing 1
error_flags: FLASH_SR bit 2 – PGERR (Programming Error): address contained value ≠ 0xFFFF before programming
FLASH_SR bit 4 – WRPRTERR (Write Protection Error): programming a write-protected address
programming.lock_mechanism: Write 1 to FLASH_CR bit 7 (LOCK) to lock; unlock requires re-writing KEY1 then KEY2 to FLASH_KEYR

option_bytes.encoding: Complemented (inverted): each 32-bit word = [nBYTE (bits 31:24) | BYTE (bits 15:0)] where nBYTE = ~BYTE. FPEC auto-computes MSB from the LSB written by software (PM §2.3.5 p.16).
layout: 0x1FFF F800: [nUSER | USER] [nRDP | RDP] – user config + read-protection
0x1FFF F804: [nData1 | Data1] [nData0 | Data0] – user data storage
0x1FFF F808: [nWRP1 | WRP1] [nWRP0 | WRP0] – write protection bytes 0-1
0x1FFF F80C: [nWRP3 | WRP3] [nWRP2 | WRP2] – write protection bytes 2-3
configurable_fields: RDP – read protection (value 0x00A5 = RDPRT key enables; 0x00FF or erased = disabled/protected)
WRP0-3 – write protection (4 bytes, 4 bits each for medium-density; 0 = protected, 1 = not protected)
option_bytes.programming_method: Unlock OPTWRE (write KEY1 then KEY2 to FLASH_OPTKEYR), set OPTPG in FLASH_CR, half-word write to target option-byte address, wait BSY clear, system reset to reload
option_bytes.erase_method: Unlock OPTWRE, set OPTER in FLASH_CR, set STRT, wait BSY clear; entire option-byte area erased to 0xFF
option_bytes.reload_trigger: System reset (or POR reset) – option bytes are reloaded by the OBL on every system reset

read_protection_states: Protected: RDP byte = 0xFF (erased state) or any value whose complement does not match
Not protected: RDP byte = RDPRT key (0x00A5), complement = 0xFF5A
security.read_unprotect_evidence: PM §2.4.1 p.17-18: 'When the Flash memory read protection option is changed from protected to unprotected, a Mass Erase of the main Flash memory is performed.' Also: 'This operation first forces a Mass Erase of the main Flash memory.'
security.write_protection_granularity_detail: 4 pages × 1 KB per WRP bit (medium-density). WRP0 covers pages 0-31, WRP1 pages 32-63, WRP2 pages 64-95, WRP3 pages 96-127. For C8 (64 KB / 64 pages), only WRP0 and WRP1 address valid pages.
security.write_protection_remove_method: Erase entire option-byte area via OPTER, then either (Case 1) program RDPRT 0x00A5 (forces mass erase) or (Case 2) leave erased, then system reset
security.write_protection_activation: Program WRP[3:0] option bytes, then apply system reset to reload

uncertainties: PM0075 §2.3.4 p.14 page-erase text states 'BSY bit in the FLASH_CR register', but BSY is defined in FLASH_SR (§3.4 p.25) and Figure 2 (p.15) and the mass-erase text (p.15) both say FLASH_SR. This is an internal inconsistency in PM0075 Rev 2. The correct register is FLASH_SR based on §3.4 and Figure 2.

external_crystal_required_for_swd_programming: Neither PM0075 nor DS5319 explicitly states whether an external crystal (HSE) is or is not required for SWD-based Flash programming. PM0075 p.10 states HSI must be ON; DS5319 §2.3.7 p.15 states HSI is the default clock on reset. From this one can infer HSE is not mandatory, but no sentence in either document says 'no external crystal is needed for SWD programming.' Marked 'unknown' to respect the no-inference rule.

required_address_alignment_bytes = 2 is derived from the half-word (16-bit) programming statement in PM §2.3.3. The document does not explicitly state an alignment requirement in bytes; it states the write is a 'half-word write at the desired address', which implies 2-byte alignment.

For C8 (64 KB / 64 pages), WRP2 and WRP3 in the option bytes address pages 64-127 which do not exist. PM0075 does not explicitly state that these bits are ignored on x8 devices; this is inferred from the fact that the device only has 64 pages. Not stated in either supplied document.

PM0075 Table 28 (p.56) lists tME (mass erase time) max as 40 ms without specifying whether this applies to 64 KB or 128 KB. The mass-erase time for C8 vs CB is not differentiated in the two supplied documents.

The 'T6' suffix decoding (T = LQFP, 6 = industrial −40/+85 °C) is from DS5319 §7 p.104. The '6' vs '7' temperature suffix distinction is also on that page. This is ordering-information, not a programming parameter, but included for completeness.
